web_evidence.title: The Bazaar of Bad Dreams | Book by Stephen King | Official Publisher Page
web_evidence.note: The publisher identifies a predominantly prose collection of twenty-one stories with separate autobiographical introductions and supplies an authorized excerpt from the non-base introduction. Collection structure does not itself make the eligible prose narratives EXCLUDED.

web_evidence.title: Stephen King | The Bazaar of Bad Dreams
web_evidence.note: The author's official catalog classifies the book as a collection containing short stories, novellas, and two poems. This is useful eligibility and contents context, but catalog description is not person evidence and does not warrant exclusion of the prose stories.

web_evidence.title: Stephen King Writing Styles in The Bazaar of Bad Dreams
web_evidence.note: The study guide explicitly says the collection employs both first- and third-person points of view and identifies the prose stories Under the Weather and Blockade Billy as first-person examples.

web_evidence.title: Stephen King | Premium Harmony
web_evidence.note: The author's official page explicitly states that the constituent story 'Premium Harmony' is told in third person, illustrating the independent narrative persons within the collection.

Adjudication follow-up searched named first-person stories including Under the Weather, Drunken Fireworks, and Blockade Billy; official pages confirmed their inclusion or audio availability, while BookRags supplied the usable explicit first-person classification.
person_note: This predominantly prose story collection is eligible for book-level classification under the same treatment applied to other collections: autonomous stories are sustained sections, not grounds for an unwritten single-narrative-only or novels-only exclusion. BookRags explicitly identifies the prose stories Under the Weather and Blockade Billy as first-person, while Stephen King's official site explicitly identifies Premium Harmony as third person. The two poems, including The Bone Church, and King's autobiographical introductions are non-base for prose-story person classification; the popularity-selected Goodreads sample is dominated by those introductions, gnomic lines, and character speech and does not independently expose a sustained first-person story passage. The reconciled result is therefore ALTERNATING at med confidence: credible Tier C named-story evidence establishes both first- and third-person prose components, but there is no Tier A/B whole-collection person analysis or independent Goodreads confirmation of both components. Adjudication: EXCLUDED was reversed because independent prose stories do not violate stated eligibility, restoring consistency with the prior classification of Squirrel Seeks Chipmunk.
